Skewered Mochi

Served at: Dondoyaki Bonfire

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 10 min

Skewered Mochi is a traditional Japanese treat enjoyed during the Dondoyaki Bonfire festival, which marks the end of the New Year celebrations. Mochi rice cakes are grilled over the bonfire, symbolizing purification and the sending off of New Year's decorations and good luck charms. This simple, warm snack is beloved for its chewy texture and slightly charred flavor.

Ingredients

  • 8 small round mochi cakes (about 1 inch/2.5 cm each)
  • 4 bamboo skewers
  • Soy sauce for brushing (optional)
  • Sugar for sprinkling (optional)

Method

  1. Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes to prevent burning.
  2. Thread two mochi cakes onto each skewer.
  3. Prepare a grill or bonfire with medium heat and embers suitable for cooking.
  4. Place the skewered mochi over the heat, turning frequently to cook evenly.
  5. Grill until the mochi puffs up and develops a light golden-brown char, about 8-10 minutes.
  6. Optionally, brush the mochi with soy sauce and sprinkle a little sugar, then grill for an additional minute to caramelize.
  7. Remove from heat and let cool slightly before serving.

Tips

  • Use fresh mochi for best texture; frozen mochi should be thawed before grilling.
  • If you don’t have access to a bonfire, a grill or broiler works well for cooking mochi.
  • Try dipping grilled mochi in sweet soy sauce or sprinkle with kinako (roasted soybean flour) for variation.
